pages.text:
March 4, 2025

Barbara Crews
Chair, Girdwood Trails Committee
PO Box 649
Girdwood, AK 99587

Dear Anchorage Assembly Members,

Girdwood was founded as a supply town for the gold fields up valley. When the gold fields played out,
Girdwood’s economy temporarily pivoted to being a supply post for the construction of the Seward Highway.
Then in 1956, the Girdwood Community Club formed the non-profit Alyeska Ski Corporation, and so began
Girdwood’s current economy based on outdoor recreation and tourism.

Girdwood’s residents and visitors alike value Girdwood’s recreational opportunities involving both Alyeska
Resort and Girdwood’s trail system. To keep Girdwood’s economy strong, we need both Alyeska and
Girdwood’s interconnected trail system.

I appreciate the efforts Alyeska Resort has made to respect the adopted Girdwood Trails Plan, which took 5
years to write and involved exhaustive public process. Alyeska has made efforts to move their Glacier Creek
development away from Stumpy’s Summer Trail and has included a massively edited version of the planned
Forest Loop Trail in their site plan. However, I am concerned that their efforts do not go far enough to protect
the trail system as envisioned in the Girdwood Trails Plan.

   •  Girdwood’s trails are public trails and they need to be on public land or on perpetual easements, so
       that the community’s investment in building trails is not in any way endangered in the future. Without
      a guarantee that the trails will be protected, there will be little interest in constructing new trails given
       the considerable time, effort, and money needed to build trails.
   •   Trails should be free to everyone who would like to use them. Girdwood does not want to become an
       exclusive community where people are blocked from accessing trails because they are on private land
       (which used to public land in this case). Alyeska Resort should be required to provide free access and
       free parking to trail users. Alyeska Resort’s guests use the trail system, so the Resort benefits from the
       considerable investment the community puts into building and maintaining its trails.
   •  The Trails Plan includes a trail that would connect the Forest Loop Trail to the Middle Iditarod Trail by
      way of a proposed bridge (B5). Although this bridge is merely conceptual at this juncture, there needs
       to be an easement provided that protects access to this bridge so that it will be possible to construct it
     when funds become available.

The Trails Committee supports the community’s public process and the S version of the Girdwood
Comprehensive Plan without amendments. However, if the Assembly plans on overriding the community’s
voice and passing Amendment 2, please consider adding some amendments to Amendment 2 which would
address the concerns I have outlined above.

Thank you for your consideration,
Barbara Crews
